title: Microburst stabilizer batcher lab notes
content:
Purpose
Quick working notes from the microburst stabilizer probe. Trying to capture intuition, experiment matrix, commands run, and early numbers. This is a messy lab notebook — rough observations, TODOs, and followups.

Background
- Problem: short-lived microbursts (tens to low hundreds of concurrent requests for ~200-800ms) cause continuous-batcher to either over-coalesce (large batches -> p99 explosion) or underfill (extra latency due to timeouts). We want to reduce p95/p99 tail while holding throughput and not regress median.
- Variability: observed especially on multi-tenant VMs where some tenants emit many short requests (chat tokens) while others emit long generation calls. Mixed token-length workload exacerbates KV-cache pressure and kernel hot-spots.

Goals (measurable)
- Reduce p99 latency for microburst traces by >= 30% vs baseline policy under controlled replay.
- Keep median change < +5ms, throughput within 98-102% of baseline.
- Avoid fairness regressions for lower-tier tenants (no tenant's p95 > +20% relative).

Hypotheses
1) Shorter max-timeout + dynamic minimum batch size adjustment keyed on arrival variance will reduce p99 by preventing over-coalescing during burst tails.
2) Introducing an urgency score (age + tenant_sla_weight) and using it in prefill ordering will avoid starvation while allowing aggressive batch growth for low-urgency requests.
3) Adaptive small-batch-prefill (fill-to-target if predicted wait < X ms) using a lightweight estimator trained on recent interarrival times will cut tail latency without hurting throughput.
4) Slightly favoring older partial batches (age multiplier 1.2) reduces tail spikes when microbursts decay rapidly.

Experiment matrix (config axes)
- timeout_ms: [6, 10 (baseline), 20]
- max_batch_tokens: [2048, 4096, 8192]
- min_batch_fill: [1, 3, 6]
- urgency_multiplier: [1.0 (baseline), 1.15, 1.3]
- prefill_strategy: [always_prefill, predicated_prefill]  # predicated_prefill = prefill only if predicted wait < 8ms
- age_bias: [1.0, 1.15, 1.3]
- fairness_mode: [soft-demote, hard-demote]  # soft-demote gently reduces priority for long-running tenants; hard-demote enforces quotas

Setup / test harness
- Use replay harness (replay-service v0.42) with clustered microburst trace (trace id: microburst-2025-01-28-17z). The trace contains mixed token lengths: 60% short (avg 12 tokens), 25% medium (avg 120 tokens), 15% long (>512 tokens).
- Run on staging dedicated GPU pool (g4dn-equivalent, 4x instances) — controlled to avoid infra noise.
- Trace duration: 10 minutes, with bursts at 0:30, 3:15, 6:40. Microburst peak concurrency ~230, baseline continuous-batcher queue length spikes to 900 tokens.
- Metrics collected: p50/p90/p95/p99 tail, token/sec throughput, kernel utilization (SM%), KV cache eviction rate, batch formation histograms, time-in-queue distributions per-tenant.

Quick commands used
- Start replay: replayctl start --trace microburst-2025-01-28-17z --policy <policy-json> --pool staging-microburst
- Trace aggregator: curl -s localhost:9090/metrics?trace_id=mic1 | jq . > mic1-metrics.json
- Microtrace dump (example): curl -s localhost:8081/microtrace?id=abc123 | sed -n '1,120p'

Observed microtrace snippets (examples)
- Example A (baseline): T=0ms reqA arrives -> waits 18ms for batch timer -> forms batch size 48 -> kernel start -> p99 for small reqs = 420ms
- Example B (timeout=6): T=0ms reqX arrives -> timer fires at 6ms -> forms batch size 6 -> pipeline start -> p99 = 310ms (reduction), but median increased by ~4ms due to more kernels invoked for small batches

Early results (not exhaustive)
- Baseline (timeout=10, min_fill=3, max_tokens=4096): p50=22ms p90=78ms p95=145ms p99=420ms throughput=100% KV-evictions=baseline
- Config A (timeout=6, age_bias=1.15, predicated_prefill): p50=26ms p90=62ms p95=110ms p99=295ms throughput=99% KV-evictions -3% -> promising (p99 -29.8%)
- Config B (timeout=20, larger batches): p99 increased to ~530ms, throughput nominally +1.5% but unacceptable tail
- Config C (urgency_multiplier=1.3 + soft-demote): p99=320ms but some low-tier tenant p95 increased by 22% -> fairness regression

Interpretation / notes
- Shortening timeout reduces over-coalescing which helps tail. But diminishing returns: too short -> worse median due to kernel-setup overhead.
- Age bias 1.15 seems to help prioritize lingering partial batches after a burst, cutting the long tail without large throughput cost.
- Predicated prefill (prefill only when predicted wait < threshold) helps in mixed workloads — prevents prefill for long-request bursts which would otherwise bloat batches with big requests.
- Fairness is brittle: urgency/weighting helps but needs tenant-aware caps. Soft-demote needs a stronger guardrail to avoid >20% regressions for low-tier tenants. Consider implementing per-tenant moving-window budget.

Open questions / TODOs
- Can we piggyback kernel batching across tiny batches (micro-kernel coalescing) to reduce per-kernel overhead? (Follow-up infra ticket)
- Need a robust predictor for predicated_prefill: explore simple EWMA interarrival estimator vs tiny NN. Which has acceptable tail risk at 99th?
- Reproduce tests on different hardware (A100 vs g4) — batch formation behavior differs; need normalized throughput/latency baseline.
- Integrate tenant budget telemetry into scheduler snapshot to enforce stronger fairness guards.

Actionable next steps (short-term)
1) Run expanded grid around timeout=6/8/10 and age_bias=1.1/1.15/1.2 with predicated_prefill using EWMA predictor. Collect 30 runs. Owner: Marco. Due: 2025-03-11.
2) Prototype per-tenant budget guard (leaky bucket) to cap soft-demote impact. Owner: Lina. PR stub: github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/914. Due: 2025-03-18.
3) Add a micro-kernel coalescing perf test to infra microbench harness. Owner: Jonah. Due: 2025-03-20.

Notes to self
- Keep snapshots of microtrace ids for any run that has p99 < 320ms. Attach to ENG ticket.
- Be wary of replay harness artifacts: ensure interarrival jitter preserved — we randomized start offsets in last run which flattened burst peaks. For fair comparison, use same seed.

Appendix: rough numeric outputs from run A (raw)
- batch-size-histogram: [1: 8%, 2-4: 35%, 5-12: 40%, 13-48: 14%, >48: 3%]
- time-in-queue-ms histogram: [0-2: 12%, 3-10: 50%, 11-30: 25%, 31-100: 8%, >100: 5%]
- kernel-util (avg SM%): 62% (spikes to 98% during long-request coalescence)

If reviewer: please ping on slack with any immediate objections. Will iterate this into a short recommended config for staging after the grid runs.

-- A.P.
